title: What should connecting look like in decade-channel?
body:
A client connects with one of two functions:

```rust
pub fn connect(path: &Path, name: &str, accepts: &[Verb], shows: &[Shows],
    pane: Option<&str>, agent: Option<&Agent>)
    -> io::Result<(Channel, Receiver<Message>)>

pub fn from_env(name: &str, accepts: &[Verb], shows: &[Shows], agent: Option<&Agent>)
    -> Option<io::Result<(Channel, Receiver<Message>)>>
```

Most callers pass `&[]` or `None` for most arguments, so a call reads as a row of blanks. `from_env` returns `None` when `DECADE_SOCKET` is unset, wrapped around an `io::Result`, so every example writes `.expect(...)?`. Neither takes a restore block (see "A client cannot send its restore block in its hello").

## Options

- A builder: `Channel::builder("name").accepts(...).shows(...).agent(...).from_env()`.
- Connecting takes a `Hello` the caller fills in with `..Default::default()`.
- Keep the functions, and make `from_env` return `io::Result` with an error kind for a missing socket.

## Open

- Should a program that decade did not start get a typed error, or `None`?
